curation.notes: Within a broader antiviral study, AFM single-molecule force spectroscopy measures unbinding of His-tagged SARS-CoV-2 spike trimer (tethered to the cantilever via maleimide-PEG/thiol-trisNTA) from surface-immobilised H84T-BanLec and from ACE2 on living VeroE6 cells, over loading rates 10-10,000 pN/s; spike variants wild type, N234Q, Delta and Omicron were compared. High-speed AFM imaging (RIBM) of spike-lectin complexation is the correlative modality; most of the paper (cell/animal antiviral assays) is not force spectroscopy.

evidence.snippet: Force distance measurements were performed at room temperature (∼25°C) using cantilevers with 0.01 N/m nominal spring constants (MSCT, Bruker) in TBS buffer containing 1mM CaCl2, and 0.1% Tween-20.

afm.cantilever_model: MSCT (Bruker) for SMFS; USC-F1.2-k0.15 (NanoWorld) for HS-AFM

evidence.snippet: Determined spring constants ranged from 0.008-0.015 N/m.

Force-distance curves were acquired by recording at least 1000 curves with vertical sweep rates between 0.5s and 10s and at a z-range of typically 500–1000 nm, resulting in a loading rate from 10–10,000 pN/s, using a commercial AFM (Keysight Technologies, USA).

the rationally engineered H84T-banana lectin (H84T-BanLec), which specifically recognizes high mannose found on viral proteins but seldom on healthy human cells
When the tip tethered molecule bound to ACE2 on the cell surface, a pulling force developed during the upward movement of the cantilever causing the cantilever to bend downwards.
VeroE6 cells were grown on Petri dishes (3 mm in diameter) using DMEM containing 10% FBS, 500 unit/mL penicillin and 100 μg/mL streptomycin at 37°C with 5% CO2.
